evals.prompt: WIP is piling up in front of Work Center B on our line. A junior planner assumes Work Center B is the bottleneck and wants to add a second machine there. Using the production-scheduling skill's bottleneck-identification approach, is that assumption safe, and what should be checked first?
evals.expected_output: Says WIP pileup does not necessarily mean that work center is the true constraint, and recommends checking the load-hours/available-hours utilization ratio and verifying causally before adding capacity.

assertions.text: Says WIP pileup doesn't prove it's the constraint
Recommends verifying utilization or a causal check

evals.prompt: Using the production-scheduling skill's Drum-Buffer-Rope framework, should a non-constraint work center be scheduled to run at 100% utilization if the constraint only runs at 85%?
evals.expected_output: Says no — non-constraint resources should be subordinated to the constraint's pace; running them at 100% while the constraint runs at 85% creates excess WIP with no throughput gain.

assertions.text: Says this creates excess WIP without throughput gain

evals.prompt: In SMED methodology as described in the production-scheduling skill, what is the difference between an internal and an external setup element, and what's the general strategy for reducing changeover time?
evals.expected_output: Explains internal elements require the machine stopped while external elements can be done while the machine still runs, and the strategy is to convert internal elements to external wherever possible.

assertions.text: Distinguishes internal vs external setup elements
